lines.text: 2 Corinthians 4: 6-тr
For it is the God who said, "Let light shine out of darkness"
who has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of
the glory of God in the face of Christ.
But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, to show that the
transcendent power belongs to God and not to us. We are
afflicted in every way, but not crushed; perplexed, but not
driven to despair; persecuted, but not forsaken; struck down, but
not destroyed; always carrying in the body the death of Jesus,
so that the life of Jesus may also be manifested in our bodies.
For while we live we are always being given up to death for
Jesus' sake, so that the life of Jesus may be manifested in our
mortal flesh.
THe cruel distress of the times through which we are living
fills our hearts with anxious questioning as we wonder how we
are to master things; it awakens in our minds desires and
hopes, it drives us to plan and scheme in the effort to sur-
mount our difficulties. "Master things", "surmount our
difficulties"—such phrases we all no doubt understand
primarily in the sense of succeeding in putting our troubles
behind us, of pulling through and extricating ourselves from
our adversities; of building a better future, if not for our-
selves, at least for our children. And of course such anxieties,
such considerations and hopes ought to have a place in our
minds; but our text teaches us that anxieties and hopes on
this plane should not be the first and most important thing
with us, that the true victory over our distresses is an inner
victory; not a future victory but an effectively present one.
The point is not how we are to remove our trials but how we
are to bear them steadfastly; not how we are to banish them,
but how we are to control and deal with them; not how
happy we shall be when they are passed, but how in the very
